summary: Archibald Amory, 58, reportedly being held in Tennessee pending return to New York, where he was tied to two casesA man has been arrested in Nashville after DNA linked him to a series of unsolved New York City rapes from the 1990s, according to a news report.Archibald Amory, 58, was detained on Thursday in Hermitage, a neighborhood of Nashville, and is being held there pending his return to New York City, according to the Daily News, citing sources and Nashville authorities.

stories.title: Peltola’s Alaska victory secures 56th Democratic seat in Senate | First Thing
summary: The ninth gain of the midterms in the upper chamber, it is the first time Alaska has elected a Democrat since 2008.
Democrats will control 56 seats in the upper chamber after the final Senate race was called in favor of Mary Peltola.

Peltola, a former US House lawmaker, is the first Democrat Alaska has elected to the Senate since 2008.Her campaign was dogged by controversy after the New York Times reported her staffers had helped recruit a second Republican challenger also named Dan Sullivan to run.

summary: A government watchdog has also labeled Hegseth’s defense policy appointee a ‘walking conflict of interest’One of defense secretary Pete Hegseth’s key advisers faces questions about potential conflicts of interest over his many roles, including advising the US defense department, Saudi Arabia, and an Israeli defence contractor.Former Republican senator Norm Coleman emerged as an informal yet omnipresent guide for Hegseth in December 2024 as the former Fox News host navigated confirmation hearings for his nomination as defense secretary.

Hegseth now finds himself under fire after articles of impeachment were filed by Republican congressman Thomas Massie charging him with “high crimes and misdemeanors,” including waging war against Iran in violation of the War Powers Act, but Hegseth’s imprint on the Pentagon goes beyond the disastrous war against Iran.

stories.title: SSE threatens to close Yorkshire gas storage site unless ministers intervene
summary: Energy firm says existing market arrangements do not sustain facility’s continued operation The energy company SSE has warned it will close its Atwick natural gas storage facility in northern England next summer, if the government does not intervene to offer support amid weak market conditions.The site, located near Hornsea on the East Yorkshire coast, consists of eight caverns with the capacity to store about 309m cubic metres of gas, estimated at about 1.5 days’ worth of Great Britain’s gas usage.
